newsitem.title: FRANCE: Small bomb explodes in Corsica.
newsitem.headline: Small bomb explodes in Corsica.

text.p: A small bomb blew up in front of a municipal building in the northern Corsican town of Ville de Pietrabugno early on Thursday, police said.

No one was injured, and no one immediately claimed responsibility for the blast, but it appeared to be the latest in a series of bombings blamed by police on Corsican separatists seeking greater autonomy from mainland France.
The Mediterranean resort island has been shaken for the past two decades by a low-level guerrilla campaign which typically strikes at government-related targets.
But attacks have become a daily occurrence since Corsica's outlawed National Liberation Front (FLNC) accused the government of wrecking a peace process and ended a truce in mid-August.
French Prime Minister Alain Juppe won backing from Corsican deputies on Wednesday for a crackdown on separatist violence.
